title: NY S00822: Relates to the disclosure of automated employment decision-making tools; requires the office of information technology services to maintain an artificial intelligence inventory; provides that the use of artificial intelligence systems shall not affect the existing rights of employees pursuant to an existing collective bargaining agreement, or the existing representational relationships among employee organizations or the bargaining relationships between the employer and an employee organization.

obligations: Any state agency that utilizes an automated employment decision making tool shall publish a list of such tools on its website no later than the thirtieth of December next succeeding the date the amendments take effect, and annually thereafter. The disclosure must include a description of the tool, the date use began, a summary of purpose and use, and any other information deemed relevant by the agency (Sec. 402).
The office shall maintain an inventory of state agency artificial intelligence systems and issue guidance to state agencies identifying data elements to be collected and submitted (Sec. 103-e).
The inventory shall be posted on the New York state open data website on the thirtieth of December next succeeding the date this section takes effect, and annually thereafter (Sec. 103-e).
State agencies shall submit information required by the office at least sixty days in advance of the annual publication date (Sec. 103-e).
The office may ask and shall receive from any state agency any information or assistance necessary to carry out its powers and duties (Sec. 103-e).
The office shall submit a copy of the artificial intelligence inventory to the governor, the temporary president of the senate, and the speaker of the assembly (Sec. 103-e).

The use of artificial intelligence systems shall not affect existing rights of employees pursuant to an existing collective bargaining agreement, or existing representational relationships among employee organizations or bargaining relationships between the employer and an employee organization (Sec. 5).

The use of such artificial intelligence systems shall not result in discharge, displacement or loss of position, including partial displacement such as a reduction in hours of non overtime work, wages, or employment benefits, or result in impairment of existing collective bargaining agreements (Sec. 5).
The use shall not result in transfer of existing duties and functions currently performed by employees of the state or any agency or public authority to an artificial intelligence system (Sec. 5).

The use shall not alter rights or benefits, and privileges, including terms and conditions of employment, civil service status, and collective bargaining unit membership status of all existing employees of the state or any agency or public authority, which shall be preserved and protected (Sec. 5).
prohibitions: Use of artificial intelligence systems shall not result in discharge, displacement or loss of position, including partial displacement such as a reduction in hours of non overtime work, wages, or employment benefits, or result in impairment of existing collective bargaining agreements (Sec. 5).
Use shall not result in transfer of existing duties and functions currently performed by employees of the state or any agency or public authority to an artificial intelligence system (Sec. 5).

Use shall not alter rights or benefits, and privileges, including terms and conditions of employment, civil service status, and collective bargaining unit membership status of all existing employees of the state or any agency or public authority (Sec. 5).

Use shall not affect existing rights of employees pursuant to an existing collective bargaining agreement, or existing representational relationships among employee organizations or bargaining relationships between the employer and an employee organization (Sec. 5).

Passed 2025-02-14. Reading generated by ollama:deepseek-v4-pro from the enrolled text; the full text is at the foot of this page so every statement can be checked against it. LegiScan record · official text

What it does

This law requires state agencies that use automated employment decision making tools to publish a list of those tools on their websites annually. It also requires the Office of Information Technology Services to maintain and publish an inventory of state agency artificial intelligence systems. It protects existing employee rights, collective bargaining agreements, and positions from being affected by the use of artificial intelligence systems.

Who it applies to

  • State agencies as defined in Sec. 401
  • The Office of Information Technology Services
  • Employees of the state or any agency or public authority
  • Employee organizations and employers in bargaining relationships

Effective date

Sections 1 through 5 take effect July 1, 2025, the same date as the 2024 chapter as amended by Sec. 6. Section 5 expires and is deemed repealed July 1, 2028. The act otherwise takes effect immediately (Sec. 7).

Key definitions

  • Automated employment decision making tool: any software that uses algorithms, computational models, or artificial intelligence techniques, or a combination, to materially automate or replace human decision making regarding employment, including wages and other compensation, hiring, selection for recruitment, discipline, promotion, and termination. It excludes basic computerized processes such as calculators, spellcheck tools, autocorrect functions, spreadsheets, electronic communications, or tools relating only to internal management affairs like ordering office supplies or processing payments, and that do not materially affect rights, liberties, benefits, safety or welfare of any individual within the state (Sec. 401).
  • State agency: any department, public authority, board, bureau, commission, division, office, council, committee or officer of the state. It does not include the legislature or judiciary (Sec. 401).
  • Artificial intelligence system: a machine based system that can, for a given set of human defined objectives, make predictions, recommendations, or decisions influencing real or virtual environments that, when used, may directly impact the public. It includes machine learning, large language model, natural language processing, computer vision, and generative artificial intelligence. It excludes basic calculations, basic automation, and pre recorded rule based conditional logic response systems with predefined triggers that automatically initiate predetermined actions, such as If This Then That systems (Sec. 103-e).
  • Directly impact the public: when the use of an artificial intelligence system would control, have a material impact on, or meaningfully influence the outcome of activities that impact the safety, welfare, or rights of the public. Such activities include assessments or decisions about individuals in law enforcement, housing, hiring and employment, financial, educational, or healthcare contexts, decisions regarding access to or eligibility for government benefits or about child welfare, or the functioning of emergency services or critical infrastructure (Sec. 103-e).

Obligations

  • Any state agency that utilizes an automated employment decision making tool shall publish a list of such tools on its website no later than the thirtieth of December next succeeding the date the amendments take effect, and annually thereafter. The disclosure must include a description of the tool, the date use began, a summary of purpose and use, and any other information deemed relevant by the agency (Sec. 402).
  • The office shall maintain an inventory of state agency artificial intelligence systems and issue guidance to state agencies identifying data elements to be collected and submitted (Sec. 103-e).
  • The inventory shall be posted on the New York state open data website on the thirtieth of December next succeeding the date this section takes effect, and annually thereafter (Sec. 103-e).
  • State agencies shall submit information required by the office at least sixty days in advance of the annual publication date (Sec. 103-e).
  • The office may ask and shall receive from any state agency any information or assistance necessary to carry out its powers and duties (Sec. 103-e).
  • The office shall submit a copy of the artificial intelligence inventory to the governor, the temporary president of the senate, and the speaker of the assembly (Sec. 103-e).
  • The use of artificial intelligence systems shall not affect existing rights of employees pursuant to an existing collective bargaining agreement, or existing representational relationships among employee organizations or bargaining relationships between the employer and an employee organization (Sec. 5).
  • The use of such artificial intelligence systems shall not result in discharge, displacement or loss of position, including partial displacement such as a reduction in hours of non overtime work, wages, or employment benefits, or result in impairment of existing collective bargaining agreements (Sec. 5).
  • The use shall not result in transfer of existing duties and functions currently performed by employees of the state or any agency or public authority to an artificial intelligence system (Sec. 5).
  • The use shall not alter rights or benefits, and privileges, including terms and conditions of employment, civil service status, and collective bargaining unit membership status of all existing employees of the state or any agency or public authority, which shall be preserved and protected (Sec. 5).

Prohibitions

  • Use of artificial intelligence systems shall not result in discharge, displacement or loss of position, including partial displacement such as a reduction in hours of non overtime work, wages, or employment benefits, or result in impairment of existing collective bargaining agreements (Sec. 5).
  • Use shall not result in transfer of existing duties and functions currently performed by employees of the state or any agency or public authority to an artificial intelligence system (Sec. 5).
  • Use shall not alter rights or benefits, and privileges, including terms and conditions of employment, civil service status, and collective bargaining unit membership status of all existing employees of the state or any agency or public authority (Sec. 5).
  • Use shall not affect existing rights of employees pursuant to an existing collective bargaining agreement, or existing representational relationships among employee organizations or bargaining relationships between the employer and an employee organization (Sec. 5).

Penalties and enforcement

The text does not state any penalties, enforcement authority, or private right of action. The office may ask and shall receive information from state agencies, and may withhold certain information if disclosure would jeopardize security of information technology assets or as prescribed by article six of the public officers law (Sec. 103-e).

How it affects AI deployment

  • State agencies that use automated employment decision making tools must publicly disclose those tools on their websites annually, including description, start date, purpose, and other relevant information (Sec. 402).
  • State agencies must report artificial intelligence systems to the office for inclusion in a public inventory posted on the New York state open data website (Sec. 103-e).
  • Artificial intelligence systems that directly impact the public, such as those used in hiring, employment, law enforcement, housing, financial, educational, healthcare, government benefits, child welfare, emergency services, or critical infrastructure, are subject to inventory reporting (Sec. 103-e).
  • Use of artificial intelligence systems cannot displace employees, reduce hours, wages, or benefits, impair collective bargaining agreements, or transfer existing duties from employees to the system (Sec. 5).
  • Existing collective bargaining rights, representational relationships, civil service status, and benefits of existing employees must be preserved and protected when artificial intelligence systems are used (Sec. 5).
  • The office may withhold certain inventory information for security reasons or under the public officers law (Sec. 103-e).

Notable exemptions

  • Automated employment decision making tool excludes basic computerized processes such as calculators, spellcheck tools, autocorrect functions, spreadsheets, electronic communications, or tools relating only to internal management affairs like ordering office supplies or processing payments, and that do not materially affect rights, liberties, benefits, safety or welfare of any individual within the state (Sec. 401).
  • Artificial intelligence system excludes basic calculations, basic automation, and pre recorded rule based conditional logic response systems with predefined triggers that automatically initiate predetermined actions, such as If This Then That systems (Sec. 103-e).
  • State agency does not include the legislature or judiciary (Sec. 401).
  • The office may withhold certain information if disclosure would jeopardize the security of information technology assets, or as prescribed by article six of the public officers law (Sec. 103-e).
  • Section 5 expires and is deemed repealed July 1, 2028 (Sec. 7).

Compliance steps

  • Determine whether any software used by the state agency qualifies as an automated employment decision making tool under Sec. 401.
  • Publish a list of such tools on the agency website by the thirtieth of December following the effective date and annually thereafter, including description, date use began, summary of purpose and use, and other relevant information (Sec. 402).
  • Identify artificial intelligence systems that may directly impact the public under Sec. 103-e.
  • Submit required data elements to the office at least sixty days before the annual publication date (Sec. 103-e).
  • Ensure that use of artificial intelligence systems does not result in employee discharge, displacement, loss of position, reduction in hours, wages, or benefits, impairment of collective bargaining agreements, or transfer of existing duties (Sec. 5).
  • Preserve existing collective bargaining rights, representational relationships, civil service status, and benefits of existing employees (Sec. 5).
  • Cooperate with office requests for information or assistance (Sec. 103-e).
